final_note: Heat kills — choose the right temperature and time.

concepts.def: High Temperature Short Time — 72 °C for 15 seconds (milk).
Heat treatment destroying all viable organisms and spores.
Time at given temperature to kill 90% of a microbial population.

walkthroughs.body_html: HTST pasteurisation heats milk to 72 °C for 15 s, killing most pathogens while preserving flavour. UHT at 135-150 °C for 1-4 s gives shelf-stable milk lasting months unrefrigerated.
Louis Pasteur demonstrated heat-treatment of wine in 1864 and milk shortly after, founding modern food microbiology. The process bearing his name has saved countless lives from milk-borne disease.
The D-value is the time at a given temperature to kill 90% of a target microbe (1 log reduction). 12D reductions (a trillion-fold) are standard for canned food botulinum control.
